Q: What is the Windows equivalent for en_US.UTF-8 locale? A:

As of 2026, Windows supports the locale name "en_US.UTF-8", along with many variations. The canonical name returned by setlocale(LC_ALL, "en_US.UTF-8") is "English_United States.utf8".

This is only backward-compatible with Windows 8 if you statically link to the C++ runtime libraries.

Q: Big O Notation - data structures A:

Big O represents how fast the time complexity of code grows as the input size of a program/method grows.

To answer your question about O(log n), sometimes programs don't necessarily have to traverse through all of the input. Most common in binary search trees, we can find values in O(log n) time through only searching through log base 2 (n) elements.

Say the input size is 8, if the code runs in O(log n) time, then with this input size, our code would have at max 3 iterations of the input since log base 2 of 8 is 3. Hope this answers your question.

Q: How to get the elements of a tuple A:

Is there a way to access elements in a tuple as if it was in a vector?

With C++ 17 you can use structured bindings. So it doesn't give you the indexing that a vector does but it is pretty nifty without having to use get or tie

tupleList = std::make_tuple(word_input, getScore(word_input));

auto [word, score] = tupleList;

std::cout<<"Basic word :"<<word << " with score "<<score<<"\n";

Q: Reading PDF, TJ operator strange encoding A:

9.x.x Interpreting Text Shown with the TJ Operator

A conforming reader shall interpret text shown with the TJ operator using the following rules, in the priority given:

Process the TJ array elements in order

The TJ operator takes an array whose elements shall be either text strings or numbers.

Text strings represent character codes to be rendered.

Numbers represent spacing adjustments in thousandths of a text space unit and shall not be interpreted as characters.

Extract character codes from string objects only

For each string element in the array, the reader shall treat the contents as a sequence of raw bytes (character codes). Numeric elements shall be ignored for the purpose of text extraction.

Decode character codes using the font in effect

The character codes obtained from each string shall be mapped to characters according to the font’s encoding mechanism:

If a ToUnicode CMap is present, it shall be used to map character codes (or CIDs) to Unicode values.

Otherwise, if the font defines an Encoding (simple fonts) or a CMap (composite fonts), that mapping shall be applied to obtain character identifiers.

Concatenate decoded characters in display order

The Unicode characters resulting from each decoded string shall be concatenated in the order they appear in the TJ array, independent of spacing adjustments.

Fallback behavior

If no ToUnicode mapping is available and the font encoding or CMap does not permit a reliable mapping to Unicode, the actual character semantics cannot be determined. In this case, a conforming reader may substitute implementation-defined placeholder characters.

NOTE

The numeric values in a TJ array affect glyph positioning only. They do not encode text content and shall not be included in the extracted string.

Q: Could not load file or assembly 'Microsoft.Practices.EnterpriseLibrary.Common, Version=6.0.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=31bf3856ad364e35' or A:

Just documenting here what happened with me.

For me the error was:

Could not load file or assembly 'Microsoft.Practices.EnterpriseLibrary.Common, Version=5.0.514.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=31bf3856ad364e35' or one of its dependencies.

This DLL was not referenced anywhere in my solution.

Turns out, there was a reference to Microsoft.Practices.EnterpriseLibrary.Data added in some other project, which has an internal dependency on the Common.dll. So, in reality this problem can happen if you are using older versions of other EnterpriseLibrary functionalities too, like Logging and Caching.
